title: Algebraic spaces over fields are universally open
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], and let $X$ and $Y$ be algebraic spaces over $\operatorname{Spec}k$ [def-trf-algebraic-space, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Give their point sets the atlas topology [def-a1-space-point-topology], and form sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Then the projection $|X\times_kY|\to|Y|$ is open: it sends every open subset to an open subset. Equivalently, the structure morphism $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is universally open, meaning open on point spaces after every algebraic-space base change. No nonemptiness, quasi-compactness, quasi-separatedness or finite-type hypothesis on $X$ or $Y$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 06DN, lemma-space-over-field-universally-open, with universal openness interpreted as openness after arbitrary algebraic-space base change.

proof.text: Choose a representable surjective etale scheme atlas $p:U\to X$ by [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Fix any scheme $V$ over $k$ and put $T=X\times_kV$. The map $a:U\times_kV\to T$ is the base change of $p$, hence representable surjective etale by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Here $U\times_kV$ is the usual scheme fibre product, also representing its sheaf fibre product. Its point map is surjective and continuous by [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus]. No finiteness assumption on either scheme is needed.

source.place: Tag 06DN, lemma-space-over-field-universally-open, proof; its scheme-test-to-space-test argument is expanded using spaces-properties.tex Tags 03H4 and 03BX.

proof.text: Let $W\subseteq|T|$ be open. Continuity of $|a|$ makes $|a|^{-1}(W)$ open in $|U\times_kV|$. The scheme projection $r:U\times_kV\to V$ is open by [lem-sc-scheme-over-field-universally-open], applied to the $k$-schemes $U,V$. Writing $t:T\to V$, the equality $r=t\circ a$ and surjectivity of $|a|$ give $|t|(W)=|r|(|a|^{-1}(W))$: lift each point of $W$ along $|a|$ for the nontrivial inclusion. Thus $|t|(W)$ is open. This proves openness when the base-change space is a scheme.

source.place: Tag 06DN, lemma-space-over-field-universally-open, proof; its scheme-test-to-space-test argument is expanded using spaces-properties.tex Tags 03H4 and 03BX.

proof.text: Now let $Y$ be any algebraic space over $k$, put $P=X\times_kY$, and write $f:P\to Y$. For open $O\subseteq|P|$, test $|f|(O)$ on any representable etale scheme map $v:V\to Y$. The pullback square has upper-left space $P\times_YV\cong X\times_kV$, by the fibre-product universal property [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]; write $b:X\times_kV\to P$ and $t:X\times_kV\to V$. By [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus], $|b|^{-1}(O)$ is open and the square is surjective onto the fibre product of point sets. Consequently $|v|^{-1}(|f|(O))=|t|(|b|^{-1}(O))$: for a point on the left choose its witness in $O$ and lift the resulting pair of points through that surjection; the other inclusion is commutativity. The right side is open by step 2. Since this holds for every such $v$, [def-a1-space-point-topology] says $|f|(O)$ is open. This applies to every $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, which is exactly the asserted universal openness.
